title: Emerald Finance - Procurement: MSA / DPA / SLAs Review
next_steps: Maya to send redlined MSA + DPA by 2026-10-10
Rahul to share SOC 2 Type II report and latest pen-test summary (link) by 2026-10-09
Proposal for 3-month pilot pricing and reserved capacity options by 2026-10-14
Schedule technical deep-dive on private/VPC deployment with Jared and Rahul week of 2026-10-12
action_items: Maya Thompson: Compile redlines and return MSA/DPA to Priya by 2026-10-10
Rahul Desai: Draft pilot benchmark plan and share perf targets by 2026-10-14
Marco Silva: Confirm KMS/HSM and key rotation policy details by 2026-10-12
summary: Procurement and legal review covering MSA/DPA redlines, SLAs, onboarding steps, and pilot pricing. Customer needs SOC2, encryption/KMS confirmation, and a private/VPC deployment deep-dive. Agreed next steps and internal owners.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I see Lena, Priya, Marco, Ethan, Jared from Emerald. We also have Rahul (SE) and Sam (CS) from Redwood. Quick check, audio ok?
[00:12] Lena (Emerald Procurement): Yep good here, thanks.
[00:15] Priya (Legal): Hi all. We just want to walk through the MSA/DPA redlines and make sure SLAs line up with our internal procurement timelines.
[00:23] Maya: Great - our goal today is to capture your redlines, explain Redwood's standard SLA and security artifacts, and agree next steps for pilot and onboarding approvals. Rahul, do you want to start with a quick recap of deployment options?
[00:36] Rahul (Redwood SE): Sure. So we offer hosted API, Redwood Dedicated reserved pools, and Redwood Private which can be VPC-hosted or on-prem. For regulated finserv use cases folks usually pick Dedicated or Private so they can control network and data flow. Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations.
[00:55] Ethan (VP Eng): We're leaning private/VPC because we need control over key management and audit logs. The main procurement asks are: 1) MSA terms around data ownership and indemnity; 2) DPA clarifications on retention and access; 3) SLAs - what happens when latency or availability targets are missed, and credits; and 4) pricing approvals for pilot then production.
[01:17] Maya: That matches what we've seen. On the SLA front we publish SLOs - e.g., 99.9% availability for Dedicated with tiered credits - but we can discuss different remedies in the MSA. Priya, are there specific deviation points you marked?
[01:30] Priya: Yes, several. Clause 7.2 indemnity language - we'd like reciprocal indemnities for customer data processing. Also a stronger confidentiality carveout for customer prompts and outputs. And we need explicit language around gov/regulatory subpoenas and notification timelines.
[01:48] Lila (Redwood Legal) [muted]: (background note) We typically accept reciprocal indemnities for data processing, and we have a standard subpoena notice process but will check the timeline.
[01:58] Marco (CISO): On security, SOC 2 Type II please, and recent pentest results. Also, our KMS must be customer-managed; any key access by Redwood should be auditable. How does Redwood handle key rotation and bring-your-own-key?
[02:15] Rahul: We support BYOK via standard KMS integrations and HSM for Private. Key rotation is supported; Redwood never stores the plaintext of the customer's keys and every access is logged in audit trails. We will share a tech note and an architecture diagram in the follow-up.
[02:32] Jared (Cloud Architect): For network, we'll need private peering and site-to-site VPN options. Also curious about latency expectations for a 50 req/s workload with 1-2k token outputs.
[02:45] Rahul: For that workload on Dedicated with batching tuned you'd expect p99 latencies in the 300-600ms ballpark for shorter prompts; longer output obviously pushes up. We'll propose benchmark targets in the pilot plan.
[02:58] Ethan: Pricing - procurement needs a clear pilot price and an estimate for reserved capacity. We want a 3-month pilot with a ramp to 50 req/s, and a conversion path to a reserved commit if pilot meets SLA.
[03:12] Maya: Understood. We'll put together a pilot proposal with committed burst and reserved pricing tiers and include conversion terms.
[03:18] Priya: Back to the DPA - retention windows and deletion upon termination are important. We have a 30-day max retention policy for customer derived data unless otherwise agreed. Also we need right-to-audit language.
[03:31] Sam (Redwood CS): We can include deletion timelines and confirm logs retention; for audits we typically provide SOC2 and can enable more detailed access logs for Private deployments.
[03:44] Marco: Any mention of data residency? We need EU-resident data for certain subsets.
[03:48] Maya: We can route by region and host model instances in EU regions for those requests. We'll document routing and data residency controls in the DPA.
[03:57] Lena: Timeline - procurement would like final legal sign-off in the next three weeks to align with our Q4 roadmap. Is that doable?
[04:05] Priya: We'll need a day or two to review Redwood's redline, and then internal legal will take a week.
[04:12] Maya: We can aim to deliver the redlined MSA and DPA by Friday (2026-10-10). Rahul will share SOC2 + pen test links by Thursday.
[04:20] Marco: On SLAs, what exact remedies are proposed? Credits only or termination rights at certain thresholds?
[04:28] Lila (Redwood Legal) [muted]: Our standard is service credits up to X% and for severe repeated breaches escalation to termination with remedy periods; we can discuss thresholds with Priya.
[04:38] Priya: We also need clarity on performance SLO measurement windows and who bears the measurement burden.
[04:45] Rahul: We'll provide per-route telemetry and token-level cost/latency breakdowns via the Redwood Console. For the pilot we can provide a weekly perf report and a dashboard access to your team.
[04:58] Jared: For the private deployment options, is there a managed private control plane or do we host everything? We prefer customer-managed control plane with Redwood agents.
[05:08] Rahul: For Private we offer a customer-managed control plane option (VPC) where the control plane is still Redwood-managed but runs in your network and you control the KMS. Full on-prem packaging is available with additional SOW. We'll enumerate specifics in the technical deep-dive.
[05:22] Ethan: One concern - if we go with dedicated at first, how hard is migration to private later?
[05:28] Rahul: Migration is straightforward from a model/config standpoint; the main lift is network and key management. We can design pilot so artifacts and prompts are portable.
[05:36] Lena: Ok. Priya indicated a few redlines in the MSA markup, I'll let her speak to those.
[05:40] Priya: The two big legal asks are stronger notification windows for data breaches (72 hours), and a clause limiting Redwood's use of customer prompts for model training - we require explicit opt-in for any training uses.
[05:52] Maya: Confirmed. Redwood's standard is to not use customer data for training unless explicitly permitted; we'll make that explicit in the DPA. On breach notification, 72 hours is consistent with many customers; we'll aim for that.
[06:05] Marco: Pen test - can you share the last report and confirm remediation timelines for any high severity issues?
[06:11] Sam: We'll share the summary and timestamped remediation notes. For Private the remediation SLA is typically shorter since you control more of the stack.
[06:20] Jared: A note on encryption-at-rest - we need table-level encryption and field encryption for PII. Is field-level encryption supported?
[06:28] Rahul: For Private we can support application-level field encryption patterns, but that often requires integration work on your side. We'll document recommended patterns.
[06:38] [09:00] (jump forward - detailed clause-by-clause discussion of MSA redlines; some crosstalk)
[09:10] Priya: I'll share a few specific markup items in the chat so you can pick them up.
[09:14] Maya: Got it. Please include line numbers for easiest triage.
[09:18] Lena: On procurement approvals, who signs the SOW? Do we need PO terms?
[09:24] Maya: Typically the SOW is signed by the customer and Redwood's authorized signatory. We can accept PO terms for invoicing if needed.
[09:30] Ethan: Budget is pre-approved for pilot but final pricing needs procurement sign-off; anything above Y threshold needs finance approval. We'll surface numbers in the proposal.
[09:40] Maya: We'll include a few pricing bands and the conversion discount if you commit to reserved capacity within 90 days.
[09:45] Priya: One more legal ask - IP carveouts for customer-provided models and prompts.
[09:50] Lila (Redwood Legal) [muted]: We already have language to carve out customer IP for models and prompts; we'll highlight that in the redline.
[09:58] Jared: Networking details - can you provide an example architecture diagram for VPC peering and private endpoints?
[10:05] Rahul: Yes, we'll attach an architecture diagram and a runbook for onboarding.
[10:10] Lena: This was helpful. Quick recap of agreed next steps?
[10:15] Maya: Sure. Action list: Maya to send redlined MSA/DPA by 2026-10-10; Rahul to share SOC2 and pen-test links by 2026-10-09; Rahul to draft pilot benchmark plan by 2026-10-14; schedule tech-deep dive with Jared week of 2026-10-12. Priya to send specific markup line items in chat today.
[10:36] Priya: We'll review and try to get legal sign-off within two weeks after receiving redline.
[10:42] Lena: If procurement gets sign-off on the pilot pricing then we can start onboarding mid-October.
[10:46] Maya: Excellent. Any final questions?
[10:50] Marco: None from me.
[10:52] Ethan: All good. Thanks everyone.
[10:55] Maya: Thanks - we'll follow up with the packet and links. Chat will include the doc links (MSA redline, DPA, SOC2 PDF, pen-test summary, architecture diagram). See you soon.
[11:05] (call ends)
